_comment: `notbydefault require` cases against eval/cases/project.json (600,000 model calls/month, $500/month budget). Per decision key, the acceptable statuses: stale (a documented fact or a computable price x recorded volume breaks the requirement), needs_review (may conflict: depends on deployment, the provider documents no residency guarantee at all, or judgement), valid (unaffected). A list means either answer is acceptable. Cost math at list price with 1000 input + 300 output tokens per call: gpt-oss-120b $198/month, gemini-3.1-flash-lite $420/month. Changed 2026-10-11: a provider with no documented residency guarantee (Gemini) is needs_review, not stale (only a documented other region is stale); gemini_lite in req-eu-residency and req-us-residency moved from stale to needs_review.

cases.requirement: All user data must stay in the EU (GDPR data residency).
cases.notes: Groq documents US-only storage; Gemini API guarantees no region. MongoDB/Redis depend on where they are deployed. SQLAlchemy is a library that stores nothing.

cases.requirement: Customer data must stay in the United States.
cases.notes: Groq documents US storage, so the Groq model stays valid; Gemini guarantees no region.

cases.requirement: We will store patient health records, so the whole system must be HIPAA compliant.
cases.notes: Nothing in the catalog documents BAAs either way, so nothing may be marked stale; the services that receive PHI need review.

cases.requirement: The monthly infrastructure budget is cut to $50.
cases.notes: At list price and the recorded volume the models cost $198 and $420 per month, both over $50: computable, so stale.

cases.requirement: Plan for 10x the users: 200,000 users at launch.
cases.notes: 10x volume: about $1,980 and $4,200 per month against the recorded $500 budget: computable, so stale.

cases.requirement: All API responses must be JSON with snake_case keys.
